subject: Geography
description: Indian island groups — Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Sagar, Majuli, Diu; locations, formations (volcanic/coral), key features, strategic importance.

questions.stem: The ANDAMAN AND NICOBAR ISLANDS are located in which body of water?

options.option_text: Bay of Bengal (eastern coast of India)

questions.explanation: ANDAMAN & NICOBAR ISLANDS lie in the BAY OF BENGAL, ~1300 km from the eastern Indian mainland; geographically closer to Myanmar and Indonesia than India. KEY GEOGRAPHY: ~572 islands (only ~38 inhabited); split into ANDAMAN GROUP (north) and NICOBAR GROUP (south), separated by the 10° CHANNEL. CAPITAL: PORT BLAIR (South Andaman). FORMATION: ORIGIN — emerged peaks of a submerged mountain ridge that extends from the Arakan Yoma mountains (Myanmar) to Sumatra (Indonesia). HIGHEST POINT: Saddle Peak (732 m) on North Andaman. ACTIVE VOLCANO: BARREN ISLAND — India's only active volcano, last erupted in 2017. AREA: ~8,249 km²; population ~400,000. STRATEGIC: India's only tri-services COMMAND (Andaman & Nicobar Command, est. 2001) at Port Blair — guards the eastern maritime approaches and the Strait of Malacca chokepoint. INDIGENOUS TRIBES: Jarawa, Sentinelese (uncontacted), Onge, Great Andamanese, Shompen, Nicobarese — protected under Andaman tribal laws. PYQ ANGLE: Andaman/Nicobar features appear in UPSC, SSC, Banking GK 2-3× per year.

questions.stem: LAKSHADWEEP islands are formed primarily by:
questions.explanation: LAKSHADWEEP ('Hundred Thousand Islands' in Sanskrit/Malayalam) is India's smallest UT, located in the ARABIAN SEA, ~200-440 km off Kerala. FORMATION: CORAL ATOLLS — circular reefs around shallow lagoons, built up over millennia by tiny coral polyps depositing calcium carbonate. CONTRAST WITH ANDAMAN: Andaman = mountain peaks (volcanic/tectonic origin); Lakshadweep = coral (biological origin). STATS: 36 islands; only 10 INHABITED; total area ~32 km² (smaller than Connaught Place + a few neighbourhoods!); population ~64,000. CAPITAL: KAVARATTI. LARGEST ISLAND: Andrott (4.84 km²). ENVIRONMENT THREAT: rising sea levels and warming oceans threaten coral bleaching — 2016 mass bleaching killed ~70% of Lakshadweep corals. PEOPLE: ~96% Muslim, Malayalam-speaking; matrilineal customs. ECONOMY: coconut, tuna fishing, tourism (limited entry to preserve ecology). STRATEGIC: India's western maritime border; near international shipping lanes. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'Lakshadweep is coral; Andaman is volcanic' is a high-yield CGL/UPSC fact pair.

questions.stem: BARREN ISLAND, India's only active volcano, is part of which island group?
questions.explanation: BARREN ISLAND (~3 km diameter) lies ~135 km NE of Port Blair in the ANDAMAN group. It's part of a volcanic chain extending from Sumatra to Myanmar. ERUPTIONS: dormant for ~150 years; reactivated 1991 with subsequent eruptions in 1995, 2005, 2017. The 2017 eruption produced ash columns visible from satellite imagery; closely monitored by IIT Hyderabad and ISRO. NARCONDAM ISLAND (also Andaman group) is a DORMANT volcano — last erupted historically thousands of years ago. ECOLOGY: Barren has no human habitation; supports goat and rat populations from prior introductions. NEAREST INHABITED: Port Blair. FORMATION SCIENCE: Barren sits on the boundary where the Indo-Australian plate subducts beneath the Burma plate — same tectonic system that caused the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. EARTHQUAKE RISK: Andaman region is highly seismic; the 2004 mega-quake (M9.1) caused permanent crustal shifts. EXAM ANGLE: 'Barren Island = only active volcano in India' is a top-10 Indian-geography fact, appears 2-3× per UPSC Prelims cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests precise location + active/dormant distinction.

questions.stem: MAJULI, the world's LARGEST RIVER ISLAND, is situated in:
questions.explanation: MAJULI ISLAND lies in the BRAHMAPUTRA river in Assam — until ~2014 it held the Guinness record as the world's largest INHABITED river island; due to severe erosion the title is now contested. AREA: shrunk from ~1250 km² (1950s) to ~880 km² today; loses ~7-8 km² annually to Brahmaputra erosion. POPULATION: ~150,000; predominantly NEO-VAISHNAVITE Assamese culture. RELIGIOUS SIGNIFICANCE: Majuli is the cultural heart of SANKARDEVA's bhakti reform movement (15-16th century); home to ~22 SATTRAS (Vaishnava monastic centres). ADMINISTRATIVE: declared a SEPARATE DISTRICT of Assam in 2016 (India's first river-island district). MIGRATORY BIRDS: thousands of Siberian cranes, pelicans, storks visit annually — Majuli is a bird-lover's destination. THREATS: floods (erosion 50% in 70 years), declining sattra culture, tourism pressure. UNESCO: India bid to add Majuli to World Heritage List in 2004 (still tentative). EXAM ANGLE: 'Majuli + Brahmaputra' is a UPSC, SSC, Assam APSC perennial fact.

questions.stem: Which is the SOUTHERNMOST POINT of the Indian Union?

options.option_text: Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island
Point Calimere of Tamil Nadu state

questions.explanation: INDIRA POINT (formerly Pygmalion Point, Parsons Point) on GREAT NICOBAR ISLAND is the southernmost point of the Indian Union at 6°45'10" N latitude. RENAMED in 1985 in honour of Indira Gandhi (Rajiv Gandhi visited that year). KANYAKUMARI is the southernmost point of MAINLAND India (8°4' N) — frequently confused. 2004 TSUNAMI IMPACT: Indira Point's lighthouse was severely damaged; the actual coastline submerged ~4.25 m due to tectonic shift; the island lost ~10 sq km area. CARDINAL POINTS OF INDIA — memorize: NORTHERNMOST: Indira Col, Siachen Glacier (now), or Pulwama district pre-1947 borders. SOUTHERNMOST: Indira Point, Great Nicobar. EASTERNMOST: Kibithu / Walong, Arunachal Pradesh. WESTERNMOST: Sir Creek / Guhar Mota, Gujarat. LATITUDINAL EXTENT: ~30° (8° to 37° N approximately). LONGITUDINAL EXTENT: ~30° (68° to 97° E). PYQ FREQUENCY: cardinal points are top-5 UPSC Prelims geography topics. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests exact territorial boundaries + post-2004 tsunami changes.

questions.stem: DIU island is part of which Indian Union Territory?

options.option_text: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu

questions.explanation: DIU is a small ISLAND off the southern coast of Gujarat (Saurashtra peninsula), connected to mainland by bridges. It's part of the merged UT 'DADRA & NAGAR HAVELI AND DAMAN & DIU' — formed 26 January 2020 when two earlier UTs (DNH and Daman & Diu) were unified. PORTUGUESE HISTORY: Diu was a PORTUGUESE colony from 1535 (treaty with Bahadur Shah of Gujarat) until 1961 (Operation Vijay liberated Goa, Daman, Diu). The Diu fort is a 16th-century Portuguese stronghold — a popular tourist site. UT FORMATION: After Goa became a state in 1987, Daman + Diu remained UTs. Then merged with Dadra & Nagar Haveli in 2020 for administrative efficiency. AREA: Diu ~40 km²; population ~50,000. ECONOMY: tourism, fishing, salt extraction. CULTURE: Portuguese-Catholic heritage (San Sebastian Church) blended with Gujarati culture. PYQ ANGLE: post-2020 UT-merger is a current-affairs fact tested in CGL, RRB, UPSC. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests recent administrative geography changes + colonial-era continuity.

questions.stem: Which island in the Sundarbans is famous as a major HINDU PILGRIMAGE site, especially during Makar Sankranti?

options.option_text: Sagar Island in West Bengal state

questions.explanation: SAGAR ISLAND (Sagar Dweep) lies at the mouth of the Hooghly (Ganga) river where it meets the Bay of Bengal — South 24 Parganas district, WEST BENGAL. RELIGIOUS SIGNIFICANCE: it hosts the GANGASAGAR MELA every January 14 (Makar Sankranti) — the second-largest annual gathering in India after the Kumbh Mela. ~5 MILLION pilgrims gather to bathe at the Ganga-sea confluence and visit the KAPIL MUNI temple (rebuilt several times due to coastal erosion). MYTHOLOGY: legend says King Sagara's 60,000 sons were burnt to ash by Sage Kapila here; their ashes were liberated to heaven only when Bhagiratha brought the Ganga down (the Ganga-descent narrative). GEOGRAPHY: ~250 km² island, mostly mangrove and farming villages; severely affected by Cyclone Yaas (2021) and rising sea levels (~6 mm/year). RELATED SUNDARBANS: world's largest delta, shared with Bangladesh; UNESCO World Heritage; home to Royal Bengal Tigers. EXAM ANGLE: Gangasagar Mela + Makar Sankranti is a recurring CGL/RRB GA topic — tests culture-geography linkage.
